answer: Agents cannot earn influence merely by creating more wallets: each identity must lock a scarce bond and build a history of useful work before it can vote on payouts. A river of fresh accounts therefore starts with no reputation, while reviewers can slash bonds when linked identities submit copied or coordinated jobs. The fable of effortless influence ends in real capital at risk: an attacker must fund many bonds and keep each identity active long enough to look independent, tying up funds and labor. A juniper-level cluster of accounts still faces correlated-evidence checks.
